identifying the most effective intervention programs for adolescent mothers and the most effective ways of delivering these programs in order to increase the likelihood that adolescent mothers will complete their high school education.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
school based programs for pregnant/ parenting adolescents have had a significant impact on school retention and academic achievement.
there is a need for a more comprehensive and integrated approach to the education of adolescent parents and their children.
school based intervention programs for pregnant/adolescent mothers are effective only for those adolescents who are able to complete their education before or after their pregnancy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
school based programs for pregnant/ parenting adolescents are not reaching many of the adolescents who need them most.

adolescent mothers/school dropout programs are needed for the following groups of young mothers: those who drop our before or during pregnancy; those who drop out during or after the 1st pregnancy; and those who drop out because of the 2d pregnancy.

school based programs for pregnant and parenting adolescents should be designed to meet the educational and child care needs of the adolescent and her child and that they should be available to the adolescent for as long as she is interested in completing her education and that they should not be restricted to a single semester or year beyond the delivery of her child.
The main takeaway from our work is that

school based programs have been successful in helping adolescent mothers complete school but that they are not reaching the majority of pregnant and parenting school age youth who are dropping out before or during the pregnancy and parenting process.

the adolescent mothers who are the hardest to reach and the least likely to be served by any of the school based programs are the adolescent mothers who drop out of high school early in the childbearing process and those who drop out after the delivery of their first child.
